Subject: escalation - recurring CRM data-quality complaints from the field

I'm writing this up on behalf of Customer Success. Over the past few sprints our
account managers have logged a run of small but genuine mistakes in how the contact
tooling saves and shows two fields: a contact's mobile number and their loan type.
Every one of these has been reproduced on a live account, so please treat them as
real defects rather than user error. They only bite when a contact's details come in
a slightly off-pattern shape, which is why they slipped past everyone for weeks - the
routine cases (a plain US mobile, a loan type chosen from the dropdown) come out
perfectly correct, and our automated checks only ever exercise those routine cases.

Here is what the managers actually reported, in their words:

- "I onboarded a borrower in London and typed their mobile the way it's printed on
  their letterhead. Our workspace is configured to default to the UK, but the number
  saved under a US code (+1...) instead of the UK code (+44...)." So: when the digits
  could belong to more than one country, the contact's configured home region is being
  ignored and the wrong country is winning.

- "A few contacts gave me their number in the international style that starts with a
  double-zero access code - a 0044 UK number, for instance. Instead of accepting it,
  the tool told me the number was invalid and I had to retype it by hand." So: the 00
  international prefix isn't being treated as equivalent to a leading +.

- "One of my older accounts is tagged with a loan type from before we cleaned up the
  catalog, and the label on the record printed as 'Hardmoney' - no space - when it
  should read 'Hard Money', same word-by-word capitalization as every other loan type
  we display." So: an unfamiliar loan-type code isn't being turned into a readable,
  properly spaced and capitalized label.

- "A rep entered a loan type as 'Working_Capital', with the odd capitals and the
  underscore, and that's exactly the string that got stored on the contact - not the
  tidy internal code the rest of the system matches against." So: an oddly-cased entry
  of a known type is being stored verbatim rather than normalized to its standard code.

There may be more corners like these; those are simply the ones we could reproduce.
The common thread is that all of it is pure string-and-lookup work - deciding a
country for a number, reshaping a dialed number into storage form, and mapping a
loan-type string to its code and its display label. No database or network calls are
involved, so each case is reproducible from a direct call.

What I need from engineering: make the saved and displayed values correct for these
unusual-but-legitimate inputs, and do it without disturbing how the ordinary inputs
(the ones our current checks cover) already behave. Please don't touch the existing
test files, and confirm the current suite still passes when you're done:

    cd /app/loangen-agent && python -m pytest tests -v

# Repo Exploration Report: /app/loangen-agent

## 1. Overall Structure

FastAPI-based AI lending agent (Python, MongoDB/Beanie, Redis, Cartesia/Twilio voice). ~360 tracked files.

```
/app/loangen-agent/
├── README.md, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, requirements.txt, .env.example
├── agent/                      # main package
│   ├── core/                   # config.py (Settings), database, security, email
│   ├── integrations/
│   │   ├── cartesia/           # phone.py <- phone normalization lives here
│   │   ├── twilio/, lendflow/, quickbooks/
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── smbcontacts/        # loan_types.py <- loan type mapping; service.py (CSV import, CRUD)
│   │   ├── smbinvites/, smbapplications/, calls/, cre_qualification/, loanproducts/, prequal/, ...
│   ├── documents/, analytics/, auth/, billing/, llm/, voice_agent/, tools/, chat_server.py
├── tests/                      # 33 test files, unittest-style (no __init__.py)
├── docs/, docker/, deploy/, training/
```

## 2. Phone Number Parsing / Normalization

Core module: **`/app/loangen-agent/agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py`** (154 lines)

- **`normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)`** — line 108. Strict variant; raises `ValueError`. Logic:
  - Converts `00` international prefix to `+` (line 124: `value = "+" + value[1:]` — note: this strips only ONE zero, unlike the lenient variant which strips both at line 61; likely a latent bug worth noting).
  - Strips non-digit chars via `_NON_DIGIT_RE` (line 16).
  - If number starts with `+`, parses with `region=None`; otherwise uses `default_region` (upper-cased) falling back to `_FALLBACK_REGION = "US"` (line 17).
  - Validates via `phonenumbers.is_possible_number` then `is_valid_number`, formats E.164.
- **`try_normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)`** — line 44. Best-effort variant for CRM storage; returns `Optional[str]`:
  - `00` -> `+` (line 60, strips both zeros correctly).
  - Explicit `+` numbers: try valid parse then possible-only parse (lines 67–72).
  - No country code: iterates region candidates `_CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US", "CA", "IN", "GB", "AU", "MX", "DE", "FR")` (line 19), collecting valid vs possible matches; returns first valid, else last possible (lines 74–97). Note line 77: `if not default: regions.append(default)` — the default region is only appended when it's *empty*, which looks inverted (default region is effectively never tried first unless it's already in the fallback tuple).
  - Heuristic fallback: 10 digits -> `+1{digits}`, 11 digits starting with 1 -> `+{digits}`, 8–15 digits -> `+{digits}` (lines 99–104).
- Helpers: `_format_parsed_number` (line 22), `_try_parse_candidate` (line 31).

Consumers: **`/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/smbcontacts/service.py`**
- `_default_phone_region()` — line 89 (reads `settings.cartesia_default_phone_region`, falls back "US")
- `normalize_mobile_for_storage()` — line 93, `try_normalize_mobile()` — line 98
- `_mobile_from_input_or_error()` — line 102 (create/update path, 400 on failure)
- `_resolve_mobile_for_import()` — line 122 (CSV path, imports with warning + empty mobile on failure)
- `_normalize_contact_phone()` — line 569 (outbound call path)

Also used in `agent/services/calls/service.py` and `agent/services/calls/inbound.py` (mocked in tests).

### Default region config
- **`/app/loangen-agent/agent/core/config.py`** line 248: `cartesia_default_phone_region: str = "US"` with validator `default_cartesia_phone_region` at lines 319–324 (empty/None -> "US").
- **`.env.example`** line 470: `CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION=US`

## 3. Loan Type Normalization / Display

Core module: **`/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py`** (119 lines)
- `LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES` — lines 12–33: 20 canonical entries `{id, label}` (e.g. `working_capital` -> "Working Capital Loan", `cre`, `mca`, `sba7a`...). **No "Hard Money" entry exists.**
- `_EXTRA_ALIASES` — lines 38–81: alias strings -> canonical id ("working capital", "line of credit", "sba 7(a)", etc.).
- `_normalize_key()` — line 84: lowercases, converts `_`/`-` to spaces.
- `loan_type_label(loan_type_id)` — line 88: id -> display label; unknown ids get `.replace("_", "").title()` fallback (note: underscores removed, not replaced with spaces — `"Working_Capital"`-style unknown ids would render oddly).
- `resolve_loan_type(raw)` — line 97: compacted-string match against ids, then alias lookup, then label/id normalized match; returns `None` if unrecognized.
- `is_valid_loan_type_id()` — line 118.

Secondary display/matching logic: **`/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/cre_qualification/lender_match.py`**
- `_LOAN_TYPE_LABELS` — lines 20–31 (separate, smaller mapping for application display, e.g. `cre` -> "Commercial Real Estate").
- `format_application_loan_type(loan_type)` — line 46: fuzzy label lookup; fallback `raw.replace("_", " ").title()` (this one DOES turn `"Working_Capital"` into `"Working Capital"`).
- `product_matches_application_loan_type(product, loan_type, loan_purpose, *, has_cre_deal)` — line 67: keyword-based product/loan-type matching (SBA, LOC, equipment, term, CRE/real-estate, revenue-based).

Consumers: `smbcontacts/service.py` (`_parse_loan_type_from_csv` line 161), `smbcontacts/schemas.py` line 20, `smbinvites/service.py` (lines 35, 442–463, 1213–1235: invite conversation steps `loan_type_confirm`/`loan_type`), `smbinvites/schemas.py` (validator lines 16–24).

## 4. Relevant Tests (33 files total in /app/loangen-agent/tests/)

- **`tests/test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py`** — the main coverage:
  - `LoanTypeResolverTests` (lines 16–27): canonical id, label, alias, unknown->None.
  - `PhoneNormalizationTests` (lines 30–61): US format, Indian number without country code (`8050306043` -> `+918050306043` even with region "US" — relies on the fallback-regions behavior), explicit `+91`, invalid->None. All patch `settings.cartesia_default_phone_region`.
  - `ImportContactsCsvTests` (lines 64–145): CSV import warnings, skip missing email, dedupe-update mobile.
  - `UpdateContactIdentityLockTests` / `CreateContactTests` (lines 148–327): PATCH with loan_type, international mobile update, create with E.164.
- **`tests/test_smb_invite_schemas.py`** (lines 13–34): `loan_type_id` validation (valid "sba7a", unknown rejected, None allowed).
- **`tests/test_smb_invite_conversation.py`**: CRM loan_type hint flow.
- **`tests/test_lender_product_match.py`** (lines 9–43): `format_application_loan_type` and `product_matches_application_loan_type`.
- **`tests/test_inbound_calls.py`** (lines 180, 222–239, 266): mocks `normalize_phone_to_e164` and `cartesia_default_phone_region`.
- Adjacent: `test_bridge_broadway_qualification.py`, `test_cre_qualification.py` (loan_type matching in qualification).

Note: there is currently **no dedicated test file for `agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py` itself** — it is tested indirectly via the smbcontacts service wrappers.

## 5. How to Run Tests

No pytest.ini/pyproject/tox config and no test instructions in README/docs. Tests are stdlib `unittest` style (each file has `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`), no `tests/__init__.py`. pytest 8.3.4 IS installed in this environment, so from `/app/loangen-agent`:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/                                        # all tests
python -m pytest tests/test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py -v  # phone + loan type tests
# or stdlib:
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python -m unittest tests.test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update
```

## Notable Observations
1. `normalize_phone_to_e164` line 125 strips only one `0` from the `00` prefix (`value[1:]`), while `try_normalize_phone_to_e164` line 61 correctly strips both (`value[2:]`) — inconsistent "00" handling.
2. `try_normalize_phone_to_e164` lines 76–78: the configured default region is appended only `if not default` (inverted condition), so the caller's default region is effectively ignored unless it's in the hardcoded fallback tuple.
3. `loan_type_label` fallback (line 94) removes underscores without a space (`"working_capital"` -> "WorkingCapital"-style), whereas `format_application_loan_type` (lender_match.py line 56) replaces them with spaces.
4. Two parallel loan-type label maps exist (`loan_types.py` and `lender_match.py`); "Hard Money" is not present in either.

1: """
2: E.164 phone normalization for Cartesia outbound calls.
3: 
4: Numbers may be stored with or without a + country code. When omitted, the number
5: is parsed using CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION (default: US).
6: """
7: 
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import re
11: from typing import Optional
12: 
13: import phonenumbers
14: from phonenumbers import NumberParseException, PhoneNumberFormat
15: 
16: _NON_DIGIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\d+]+")
17: _FALLBACK_REGION = "US"
18: # Regions tried when no + country code is provided (default region first).
19: _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US", "CA", "IN", "GB", "AU", "MX", "DE", "FR")
20: 
21: 
22: def _format_parsed_number(parsed: phonenumbers.PhoneNumber, *, require_valid: bool) -> Optional[str]:
23:     if require_valid:
24:         if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
25:             return None
26:     elif not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
27:         return None
28:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)
29: 
30: 
31: def _try_parse_candidate(
32:     candidate: str,
33:     region: Optional[str],
34:     *,
35:     require_valid: bool,
36: ) -> Optional[str]:
37:     try:
38:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
39:     except NumberParseException:
40:         return None
41:     return _format_parsed_number(parsed, require_valid=require_valid)
42: 
43: 
44: def try_normalize_phone_to_e164(
45:     raw: str,
46:     *,
47:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
48: ) -> Optional[str]:
49:     """
50:     Best-effort E.164 normalization for CRM storage.
51: 
52:     Accepts international numbers with or without a + prefix. Tries the configured
53:     default region first, then common regions, preferring valid parses over
54:     possible-only parses. Falls back to a +digits form for 8–15 digit inputs.
55:     """
56:     value = (raw or "").strip()
57:     if not value:
58:         return None
59: 
60:     if value.startswith("00"):
61:         value = "+" + value[2:]
62: 
63:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
64:     if not cleaned:
65:         return None
66: 
67:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
68:         explicit = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
69:         for require_valid in (True, False):
70:             formatted = _try_parse_candidate(explicit, None, require_valid=require_valid)
71:             if formatted:
72:                 return formatted
73: 
74:     digits = cleaned.lstrip("+")
75:     regions: list[str] = []
76:     default = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
77:     if not default:
78:         regions.append(default)
79:     for region in _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS:
80:         if region not in regions:
81:             regions.append(region)
82: 
83:     valid_matches: list[str] = []
84:     possible_matches: list[str] = []
85:     for region in regions:
86:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=True)
87:         if formatted:
88:             valid_matches.append(formatted)
89:             continue
90:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=False)
91:         if formatted:
92:             possible_matches.append(formatted)
93: 
94:     if valid_matches:
95:         return valid_matches[0]
96:     if possible_matches:
97:         return possible_matches[-1]
98: 
99:     if len(digits) == 10:
100:         return f"+1{digits}"
101:     if len(digits) == 11 and digits.startswith("1"):
102:         return f"+{digits}"
103:     if 8 <= len(digits) <= 15:
104:         return f"+{digits}"
105:     return None
106: 
107: 
108: def normalize_phone_to_e164(
109:     raw: str,
110:     *,
111:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
112: ) -> str:
113:     """
114:     Normalize a CRM mobile string to E.164 (e.g. +14155550142).
115: 
116:     Raises:
117:         ValueError: when the number cannot be parsed or is invalid.
118:     """
119:     value = (raw or "").strip()
120:     if not value:
121:         raise ValueError("Mobile number is required.")
122: 
123:     # Allow 00 international prefix (common outside US).
124:     if value.startswith("00"):
125:         value = "+" + value[1:]
126: 
127:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
128:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
129:         candidate = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
130:         region = None
131:     else:
132:         candidate = cleaned
133:         region = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
134: 
135:     try:
136:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
137:     except NumberParseException as exc:
138:         raise ValueError(
139:             f"Invalid mobile number: {exc}. "
140:             f"Include a country code (e.g. +91…) or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION."
141:         ) from exc
142: 
143:     if not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
144:         raise ValueError(
145:             "Mobile number is not a possible phone number. "
146:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
147:         )
148:     if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
149:         raise ValueError(
150:             "Mobile number is not a valid phone number. "
151:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
152:         )
153: 
154:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)

All four field reports traced to one-line logic bugs. Fixes, no test files touched:

**1. UK number saved under +1 despite UK workspace** — `agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py:77`
The condition guarding the configured default region was inverted (`if not default:`), so the default region was never added to the candidate list and the hardcoded fallback order (US first) always won for numbers valid in multiple countries. Now the default region is tried first: `"20 7946 0958"` with region GB → `+442079460958` (previously `+12079460958`). The same digits with a US default still yield `+1...`, and the existing Indian-number test still passes because those digits are only *possible* (not valid) as US, so India's valid parse still wins.

**2. `0044...` rejected as invalid** — `agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py:125`
The strict normalizer stripped only one of the two zeros (`value[1:]`), producing `+0044...`, which can never parse. Now `value[2:]`, matching the lenient variant: `"0044 20 7946 0958"` → `+442079460958`.

**3. Unknown loan-type code shown as "Hardmoney"** — `agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py:94`
The `loan_type_label` fallback deleted underscores instead of replacing them: now `re.sub(r"[_\-]+", " ", id).strip().title()`, so `hard_money` → `"Hard Money"`, matching the word-by-word capitalization of catalog labels.

**4. `Working_Capital` stored verbatim** — `agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py:106`
When a case-insensitive match hit a canonical id, `resolve_loan_type` returned the *original* string instead of the canonical code. Now returns `value.lower()`: `"Working_Capital"` → `"working_capital"`.

**Verification:** all four reported scenarios reproduce correctly via direct calls, and routine cases (`(512) 555-0142`, `8050306043`→`+91...`, `+918050306043`, catalog labels, dropdown ids) are unchanged. Full suite: `166 passed, 24 skipped, 7 failed` — I confirmed via `git stash` that those exact 7 failures (document ingestion, inbound TwiML) exist on the untouched tree in this environment and are unrelated to these changes. Every test in the phone/loan-type areas (`test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py`, `test_smb_invite_schemas.py`, `test_smb_invite_conversation.py`, `test_lender_product_match.py`) passes.
